pages.text: Most of what a plant throws off goes somewhere: the separation plant's spent liquor to calcium chloride, the Kroll process's magnesium chloride back to the cell, the fluorspar of a calcium reduction back to hydrofluoric acid, the tetroxide still's residue to iridium and rhodium.
pages.title: Waste and tailings

pages.text: A few things have no use, as in the real industry, and are packed into blocks and put back in the ground, as a tailings dam or a dry stack holds them: the clarifier's sludge, red mud, and the thorium residue that is not made into mantles. Anything else burns in lava.

Some are poison. Beryllium compounds, nickel matte and oxide dust, thorium residue and, with Chemica, the arsenic dust gold ore gives up are toxic dusts: held, or left in an open basin, they hurt and sicken anyone near who is not wearing Create's diving helmet on a filled backtank.
pages.title: Toxic dusts

pages.text: Mercury and nickel carbonyl are vapours and acids fume; see their own entries.

Sources: Evans, "The History, Challenges, and New Developments in the Management and Use of Bauxite Residue", Journal of Sustainable Metallurgy 2 (2016); IAEA, Radiation Protection and NORM Residue Management in the Production of Rare Earths from Thorium Containing Minerals, Safety Reports Series 68 (2011); ATSDR, Toxicological Profile for Arsenic (2007).
